lede: The biggest thing on the docket this week is Town Council's June 30 first reading of Land Use Code amendments tied to Colorado's Wildfire Resiliency Code — a change that will shape how development and fire risk are managed in this canyon for a long time. Also on June 30, the Telluride Housing Authority takes up the structure of its new Resident Advisory Committee. On the 25th, the Hospital District board digs into mill levy considerations while the Planning and Zoning Commission holds a work session on the Shandoka Lot redevelopment.

notable.stake: First reading of wildfire code amendments sets lasting development and fire-risk rules.
Mill levy discussion could affect how the hospital district is funded by taxpayers.
Commission feedback on Shandoka redevelopment shapes a major Town-owned project's direction.
